lessons.incorrectFeedback: The filtering pattern after for is introduced by case.

lessons.title: For-Case with Where
lessons.objective: Combine sequence pattern filtering with a Boolean condition.
lessons.instruction: Visit only points on either diagonal through the origin.
lessons.codePrefix: for case let (x, y) in points
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. where adds the diagonal condition after the for-case pattern.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A for-case constraint uses where.

lessons.title: Continue
lessons.objective: Skip the remainder of the current loop iteration.
lessons.instruction: Ignore vowels and continue with the next Character.
lessons.codePrefix:
for character in input {
    if vowels.contains(character) {
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. continue ends only the current iteration and starts the next one.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: break ends the whole loop. Use continue to skip only this Character.

lessons.title: Break in a Loop
lessons.objective: End the nearest loop immediately.
lessons.instruction: Stop searching after the first matching item.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. break ends the loop and resumes after its closing brace.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: continue would keep searching. Use break once the target is found.
lessons.sourceTitle: Control Flow · Break in a Loop Statement

lessons.title: Break in a Switch
lessons.objective: Write an intentionally empty switch case body.
lessons.instruction: Do nothing for unsupported symbols while keeping every case body nonempty.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. break makes the default case intentionally perform no work.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: continue applies to loops. Use break for an empty switch case body.
lessons.sourceTitle: Control Flow · Break in a Switch Statement

lessons.title: Explicit Fallthrough
lessons.objective: Continue execution into the next switch case body explicitly.
lessons.instruction: After identifying a prime number, also run the default description body.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. fallthrough enters the next case body without checking that case's pattern.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: continue belongs to loops. Use fallthrough for explicit switch continuation.

lessons.title: Labeled Statements
lessons.objective: Target an outer loop from inside nested control flow.
lessons.instruction: End gameLoop from inside the nested switch.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. break gameLoop exits the specifically labeled while loop.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An unlabeled break exits only the switch here. Name gameLoop to exit the outer loop.

lessons.title: Early Exit with Guard
lessons.objective: Require a condition and exit the scope when it fails.
lessons.instruction: Unwrap name for use throughout the rest of the function.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. guard requires the binding and makes name available after the guard statement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An if-let binding is scoped to its branch. Use guard for early exit and later access.

lessons.title: Deferred Actions
lessons.objective: Run cleanup when execution leaves the current scope.
lessons.instruction: Schedule score restoration after all other work in this scope.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. defer schedules its body when control leaves the enclosing scope.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: guard checks a condition and exits on failure. Use defer for scope-exit cleanup.

lessons.title: Multiple Defer Order
lessons.objective: Predict last-in-first-out execution of defer blocks.
lessons.instruction: Choose which deferred message prints first.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Multiple defer blocks execute in reverse order of registration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: defer blocks use last-in-first-out order, so the second registered block runs first.

lessons.title: Checking API Availability
lessons.objective: Guard newer platform APIs with #available.
lessons.instruction: Enter the branch only where all listed minimum platform versions are available.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #available is true when the running platform meets the listed version requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #unavailable identifies older systems. Use #available for the new-API branch.

lessons.title: Checking API Unavailability
lessons.objective: Run fallback code only on systems below a required version.
lessons.instruction: Choose the condition that identifies systems where the newer iOS API isn't available.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #unavailable is true when the running platform is below the listed version.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #available selects systems that meet the version. Use #unavailable for fallback code.

levels.title: Level 6 · Functions
levels.summary: Design clear APIs and pass behavior as values.

lessons.title: Defining and Calling Functions
lessons.objective: Declare a named function with one parameter and a return value.
lessons.instruction: Choose the keyword that declares greet.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. func introduces a named function declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: let binds a value. Use func to declare a named function.

lessons.title: Functions Without Parameters
lessons.objective: Call a function whose parameter list is empty.
lessons.instruction: Invoke sayHelloWorld and store its returned String.
lessons.codePrefix:
func sayHelloWorld() -> String { "hello, world" }
let greeting =
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Empty parentheses call the no-parameter function and produce its String.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The bare name is the function value itself. Add () to call it.

lessons.title: Functions with Multiple Parameters
lessons.objective: Supply every labeled argument in declaration order.
lessons.instruction: Call greet for Anna and report that she was already greeted.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The call supplies values for both declared parameters with their labels.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The function requires alreadyGreeted as well as person.

lessons.title: Functions Without Return Values
lessons.objective: Declare a function whose explicit result type is Void.
lessons.instruction: Print a greeting and declare the equivalent explicit result type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. -> Void explicitly states the same result type a function has when its return annotation is omitted.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A String-returning function must produce a String. This function only performs printing, so its explicit result is Void.

lessons.title: Multiple Return Values
lessons.objective: Return several related values in a named tuple.
lessons.instruction: Declare minMax to return named minimum and maximum values.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A named tuple returns both Int values with min and max member access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An Array doesn't guarantee exactly two named results. Use a named tuple.
lessons.sourceTitle: Functions · Functions with Multiple Return Values

lessons.title: Optional Tuple Return Types
lessons.objective: Represent absence of the entire multi-value result.
lessons.instruction: Return nil for an empty input or one complete min-max tuple otherwise.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The ? applies to the whole tuple, so the function returns either both values or nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A tuple of optionals always returns a tuple. Make the complete tuple optional instead.

lessons.title: Implicit Function Returns
lessons.objective: Omit return from a single-expression function body.
lessons.instruction: Choose the valid body expression for a concise String-returning function.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A single expression can implicitly return its String value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: print returns Void. The body must produce the declared String.
lessons.sourceTitle: Functions · Functions with an Implicit Return

lessons.title: Custom Argument Labels
lessons.objective: Use one name at the call site and another inside the function.
lessons.instruction: Make the call read greet(person:from:) while using hometown inside the body.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. from is the external argument label and hometown is the internal parameter name.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: _ would omit the label. Use from to make the call read naturally.

lessons.title: Omitting Argument Labels
lessons.objective: Remove an external argument label with _.
lessons.instruction: Allow double(4) instead of double(value: 4).
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. _ suppresses the argument label at the call site.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Using value as the external label requires double(value:). Use _ for double(4).

lessons.title: Default Parameter Values
lessons.objective: Provide a parameter value that callers may omit.
lessons.instruction: Use 12 when the caller doesn't supply count.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. = 12 declares the default argument value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: == compares values. Use = to declare the parameter default.

lessons.title: Variadic Parameters
lessons.objective: Accept zero or more values of one parameter type.
lessons.instruction: Allow arithmeticMean to receive any number of Double arguments.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Double... lets callers pass a comma-separated variable number of Double arguments.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: [Double] requires callers to pass one Array. Use Double... for variadic arguments.

lessons.title: In-Out Parameters
lessons.objective: Allow a function to modify a caller-owned variable.
lessons.instruction: Declare a as an in-out Int so assignments update the caller's variable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. inout permits the function body to write back through the parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Ordinary parameters are constants inside the function. Mark the parameter inout.

lessons.title: Passing In-Out Arguments
lessons.objective: Pass a mutable variable to an in-out parameter with &.
lessons.instruction: Let swapTwoInts exchange the two caller variables.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. & marks a variable passed to an in-out parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses & at the call site for in-out arguments.

lessons.title: Function Types
lessons.objective: Describe a function by parameter and return types.
lessons.instruction: Declare the type of a function that accepts two Int values and returns Int.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The arrow separates the function's parameter types from its return type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: (Int, Int) is only a tuple type. Add -> Int to describe the function result.

lessons.title: Using Function Values
lessons.objective: Assign a compatible named function to a variable.
lessons.instruction: Store addTwoInts itself without calling it.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The bare function name is a value with a compatible function type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Parentheses call a function and would require arguments. Assign the function name itself.

lessons.title: Function Types as Parameters
lessons.objective: Inject behavior through a function-typed parameter.
lessons.instruction: Declare operation as a function accepting two Int values and returning Int.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The parameter can receive any function with that signature.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An Int isn't callable. Use the compatible function type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Functions · Function Types as Parameter Types

lessons.title: Function Types as Return Types
lessons.objective: Return selected behavior from a function.
lessons.instruction: Declare chooseStep to return a function that transforms one Int into another.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. chooseStep returns one of two compatible (Int) -> Int function values.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The branches are functions rather than Int results. Return the function type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Functions · Function Types as Return Types

lessons.title: Nested Functions
lessons.objective: Hide helper functions inside the scope that uses them.
lessons.instruction: Choose the declaration that can be defined locally and returned as a function value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A func declaration can be nested inside another function and returned from it.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: return exits the function. Declare the local helper with func.

levels.title: Level 7 · Closures
levels.summary: Write concise behavior values and control their lifetime.

lessons.title: Sorting with a Comparator
lessons.objective: Provide sorted(by:) a function that orders two elements.
lessons.instruction: Sort names in descending lexicographic order.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. backward returns true when its first String should appear before the second in descending order.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: < sorts comparable values ascending. Use the descending comparator.

lessons.title: Closure Expression Syntax
lessons.objective: Separate closure parameters from its body with in.
lessons.instruction: Complete the explicitly typed descending closure.
lessons.codePrefix: let reversed = names.sorted(by: { (first: String, second: String) -> Bool
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. in ends the closure signature and begins its body.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: where adds constraints elsewhere. Closure parameters and result type are followed by in.

lessons.title: Inferring Closure Types
lessons.objective: Omit closure parameter and return types when context supplies them.
lessons.instruction: Use sorted(by:)'s expected signature to infer both String parameters and Bool result.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Context infers first and second as String and the closure result as Bool.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Closure parameters are listed directly before in here rather than as one tuple parameter.

lessons.title: Implicit Closure Returns
lessons.objective: Return a single closure expression without return.
lessons.instruction: Choose the one expression that supplies sorted(by:)'s Bool result.
lessons.codePrefix: let reversed = names.sorted(by: { first, second in
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A single expression implicitly returns its Bool value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: print returns Void. The sorting closure must produce Bool.

lessons.title: Shorthand Closure Arguments
lessons.objective: Refer to inferred closure parameters as $0 and $1.
lessons.instruction: Write the descending comparison without a parameter list or in.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. $0 and $1 name the first and second inferred arguments.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: $0 < $1 sorts ascending. Use > for descending order.

lessons.title: Operators as Closure Values
lessons.objective: Pass a compatible operator implementation directly.
lessons.instruction: Use String's greater-than operator as the descending comparator.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. > has the compatible (String, String) -> Bool function type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: + returns a String rather than Bool. Pass > as the comparator.

lessons.title: Trailing Closures
lessons.objective: Move a final closure argument after the call's parentheses.
lessons.instruction: Sort names using trailing-closure syntax.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. sorted { ... } uses the final closure outside parentheses and returns a new Array.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: sort mutates a variable in place. Use sorted for this let result.

lessons.title: Multiple Trailing Closures
lessons.objective: Label trailing closure arguments after the first.
lessons.instruction: Supply a success closure followed by the labeled failure closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The first trailing closure omits its label and the following closure uses onFailure:.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The first closure already supplies completion. Label the second one onFailure:.

lessons.title: Transforming Values with Map
lessons.objective: Use a trailing closure to produce one output for every input element.
lessons.instruction: Convert every Int into its String representation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. map(_:) calls the closure once per element and collects the transformed String values.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: filter retains original elements based on Bool. Use map to change Int into String.

lessons.title: Capturing Values
lessons.objective: Preserve and mutate surrounding state across closure calls.
lessons.instruction: Complete the captured update so each call adds amount to runningTotal.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The closure captures runningTotal and amount and preserves the updated total between calls.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: == only compares. Use += to mutate the captured running total.

lessons.title: Closures Are Reference Types
lessons.objective: Recognize shared captured state after assigning a closure.
lessons.instruction: Both names reference the same incrementer. Choose the next result after one call through each name.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Both constants reference the same closure and its captured runningTotal.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Assigning a closure doesn't copy its captured state. The shared total advances to 20.

lessons.title: Escaping Closures
lessons.objective: Mark a closure parameter that can outlive the function call.
lessons.instruction: Store completionHandler in a global Array for later execution.
lessons.codePrefix:
var handlers: [() -> Void] = []
func register(_ completionHandler:
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @escaping permits storing the closure for use after register returns.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @autoclosure changes expression wrapping. Use @escaping for a closure that outlives the call.

lessons.title: Self in Escaping Closures
lessons.objective: Make instance capture explicit inside an escaping closure.
lessons.instruction: Update the instance property from a stored escaping closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Explicit self documents that the escaping closure captures the instance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The property assignment needs an explicit self reference in this escaping closure.

lessons.title: Autoclosures
lessons.objective: Delay evaluation of an expression without caller braces.
lessons.instruction: Allow serve(customer:) to receive customers.removeFirst() as a lazily evaluated expression.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @autoclosure wraps the caller's expression and delays it until provider() runs.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @escaping controls lifetime but doesn't remove caller closure syntax. Use @autoclosure.

lessons.title: Escaping Autoclosures
lessons.objective: Store a lazily wrapped expression for later evaluation.
lessons.instruction: Allow the autoclosure provider to be appended to customerProviders.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The provider is both automatically created and stored beyond the call, so it needs @escaping @autoclosure.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A nonescaping closure can't be stored. Add @escaping before @autoclosure.

levels.title: Level 8 · Enumerations
levels.summary: Model finite states with payloads, raw representations, and recursion.

lessons.title: Enumeration Syntax
lessons.objective: Declare a finite set of related cases.
lessons.instruction: Choose the declaration keyword for CompassPoint.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. enum declares a type with a finite group of cases.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: struct models stored properties. Use enum for named alternatives.

lessons.title: Inferred Enumeration Cases
lessons.objective: Omit the enumeration type when context already determines it.
lessons.instruction: Change directionToHead from west to east using concise case syntax.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The leading dot uses the known CompassPoint context.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An enum case needs its type or leading-dot contextual syntax. Use .east.

lessons.title: Matching Enumeration Values
lessons.objective: Match enum cases exhaustively in a switch.
lessons.instruction: Match the south case using type-inferred case syntax.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. .south matches the CompassPoint case rather than text.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The switched value is CompassPoint, not String. Match .south.

lessons.title: Iterating Enumeration Cases
lessons.objective: Synthesize a collection of every case with CaseIterable.
lessons.instruction: Enable Beverage.allCases for an enum without associated values.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. CaseIterable synthesizes the static allCases collection.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Sequence requires iteration implementation. Use CaseIterable for all enum cases.

lessons.title: Declaring Associated Values
lessons.objective: Attach case-specific payload types to enum cases.
lessons.instruction: Declare qrCode with one String payload.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Parentheses declare a case-specific associated String value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Raw-value syntax assigns one shared raw type to the enum. Use (String) for this case payload.

lessons.title: Creating Associated-Value Cases
lessons.objective: Construct an enum case with its required payload.
lessons.instruction: Replace the barcode with a QR-code String payload.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The qrCode case requires its associated String at construction.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: qrCode has a required associated value. Supply it in parentheses.

lessons.title: Binding Associated Values
lessons.objective: Extract an enum payload through pattern matching.
lessons.instruction: Match a QR-code barcode and bind its product code.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. let binds the associated String from the matched qrCode case.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A String literal matches only that exact payload. Use let to extract any QR code.

lessons.title: Raw Values
lessons.objective: Assign one same-typed raw value to each enum case.
lessons.instruction: Declare a Character-backed enum for ASCII control characters.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. : Character declares a common raw-value type for every case.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: (Character) is associated-value syntax. Use : Character for raw values.

lessons.title: Implicit Integer Raw Values
lessons.objective: Predict automatic integer increments after an explicit starting raw value.
lessons.instruction: Mercury starts at one. Choose Earth's implicit raw value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Integer raw values increment by one: mercury 1, venus 2, earth 3.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Venus receives 2, so Earth receives 3.

lessons.title: Implicit String Raw Values
lessons.objective: Use a case name as its implicit String raw value.
lessons.instruction: Choose the raw value of CompassPoint.south.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An implicit String raw value is the case name itself.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The case is spelled south with a lowercase s, so its raw value is "south".

lessons.title: Initializing from a Raw Value
lessons.objective: Handle the optional result of raw-value enum initialization.
lessons.instruction: Create the possible planet whose raw Int is seven.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Planet(rawValue:) returns Planet? because an arbitrary raw value may match no case.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Raw-value enum initialization uses the rawValue: label.
lessons.sourceTitle: Enumerations · Initializing from a Raw Value

lessons.title: Recursive Enumerations
lessons.objective: Permit an enum case to contain another value of the same enum.
lessons.instruction: Mark the recursive addition case so its size can be represented indirectly.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. indirect inserts the needed indirection for a recursive case payload.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses indirect rather than recursive for recursive enum storage.

levels.title: Level 9 · Structures and Classes
levels.summary: Choose value or reference semantics and construct custom types.

lessons.title: Structure Definitions
lessons.objective: Declare a structure with stored properties.
lessons.instruction: Choose the keyword that gives Resolution value semantics.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. struct declares a value type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: class declares a reference type. Use struct for Resolution.

lessons.title: Class Definitions
lessons.objective: Declare a class with reference semantics.
lessons.instruction: Choose the keyword that makes VideoMode a reference type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. class instances share reference identity.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: struct has value semantics. Use class for reference semantics.

lessons.title: Creating Instances
lessons.objective: Create an instance with initializer syntax.
lessons.instruction: Create a Resolution using its default initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Parentheses call the initializer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Resolution alone names the type. Call Resolution().
lessons.sourceTitle: Structures and Classes · Structure and Class Instances

lessons.title: Property Access
lessons.objective: Read a stored property with dot syntax.
lessons.instruction: Read the width stored inside someResolution.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Dot syntax accesses a named property.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Stored properties use dot syntax here.

lessons.title: Memberwise Initialization
lessons.objective: Initialize a structure by naming its stored members.
lessons.instruction: Create a 640 by 480 Resolution.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Structures synthesize a memberwise initializer with property labels.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The synthesized memberwise initializer uses width: and height: labels.
lessons.sourceTitle: Structures and Classes · Memberwise Initializers for Structure Types

lessons.title: Value-Type Copies
lessons.objective: Recognize independent copies of structures and enumerations.
lessons.instruction: Copy hd before changing cinema.width.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Assigning a structure copies its value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Ordinary structure assignment uses value-copy semantics; & is for in-out arguments.
lessons.sourceTitle: Structures and Classes · Structures and Enumerations Are Value Types

lessons.title: Reference-Type Sharing
lessons.objective: Recognize shared class instances.
lessons.instruction: Create another reference to tenEighty.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Class assignment shares the same instance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: VideoMode() creates a distinct instance. Assign tenEighty to share it.
lessons.sourceTitle: Structures and Classes · Classes Are Reference Types

lessons.title: Identity Operators
lessons.objective: Test whether two references identify the same class instance.
lessons.instruction: Check that tenEighty and alsoTenEighty are identical instances.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. === compares class-instance identity.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: == tests value equality when defined. Use === for identity.

levels.title: Level 10 · Properties
levels.summary: Store, compute, observe, wrap, and share values on types.

lessons.title: Stored Properties
lessons.objective: Store mutable state in a type.
lessons.instruction: Make currentLength independently mutable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. var declares a mutable stored property.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: let prevents reassignment after initialization. Use var.

lessons.title: Constant Structure Instances
lessons.objective: Understand mutation through a constant value-type instance.
lessons.instruction: Choose the declaration that permits changing range.currentLength.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A structure instance must be var to mutate any of its properties.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A let-bound structure is entirely immutable, even when a property is declared var.
lessons.sourceTitle: Properties · Stored Properties of Constant Structure Instances

lessons.title: Lazy Stored Properties
lessons.objective: Delay a stored property's initial value until first access.
lessons.instruction: Delay importer creation until dataManager.importer is first read.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. lazy defers initialization until first access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: get belongs to computed properties. Use lazy on this stored property.

lessons.title: Computed Properties
lessons.objective: Derive a value with getter and setter logic.
lessons.instruction: Start the accessor that returns an origin-derived center.
lessons.codeSuffix:
{ Point(x: origin.x + size.width / 2, y: origin.y + size.height / 2) }
}
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. get computes the property's read value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: willSet observes storage changes. A computed read accessor uses get.

lessons.title: Shorthand Setter
lessons.objective: Use the default newValue parameter in a computed setter.
lessons.instruction: Move origin using the setter's implicit incoming value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. newValue is the setter's implicit parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: oldValue belongs to property observers. Setters receive newValue.

lessons.title: Shorthand Getter
lessons.objective: Use a single expression as an implicit getter return.
lessons.instruction: Complete the read-only computed property body.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A single-expression getter returns its expression implicitly.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A computed property doesn't assign itself. Return the expression directly.

lessons.title: Read-Only Computed Properties
lessons.objective: Declare a computed property without a setter.
lessons.instruction: Choose the declaration that exposes volume as read-only.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Computed properties use var even when read-only.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: let is for stored constants. Computed properties are declared with var.

lessons.title: Property Observers
lessons.objective: React immediately before or after a stored value changes.
lessons.instruction: Observe the new totalSteps after assignment.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. didSet runs after storage changes and exposes oldValue.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: willSet runs before assignment and exposes newValue. Use didSet for oldValue.

lessons.title: Property Wrappers
lessons.objective: Reuse storage-management logic through an attribute.
lessons.instruction: Apply TwelveOrLess to height.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @WrapperType applies property-wrapper storage behavior.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Property wrappers use attribute syntax, not inheritance.

lessons.title: Wrapped Initial Values
lessons.objective: Initialize wrapper storage from the property's declaration.
lessons.instruction: Start the wrapped height at one.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The property value feeds the wrapper's wrappedValue initializer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Assign the wrapped value, not a wrapper instance, at the property declaration.
lessons.sourceTitle: Properties · Setting Initial Values for Wrapped Properties

lessons.title: Projected Values
lessons.objective: Access auxiliary wrapper state with dollar-sign syntax.
lessons.instruction: Read the projected flag associated with height.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. $height accesses the wrapper's projectedValue.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: height reads wrappedValue. Use $height for projectedValue.
lessons.sourceTitle: Properties · Projecting a Value From a Property Wrapper

lessons.title: Global and Local Variables
lessons.objective: Apply stored and computed behavior outside type properties.
lessons.instruction: Declare a computed local variable that doubles base.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Local computed variables use var with an accessor body.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A computed variable is declared with var.

lessons.title: Type Property Syntax
lessons.objective: Attach one property to the type instead of each instance.
lessons.instruction: Declare a shared stored property on a structure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. static attaches the property to the type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: mutating affects value-type methods. Type properties use static.

lessons.title: Using Type Properties
lessons.objective: Read or write a type property through its type name.
lessons.instruction: Read AudioChannel.maxInputLevelForAllChannels.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Type properties are accessed on the type itself.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: No instance is needed. Access the static property through AudioChannel.
lessons.sourceTitle: Properties · Querying and Setting Type Properties

levels.title: Level 11 · Methods
levels.summary: Define instance, mutating, and type-level behavior.

lessons.title: Instance Methods
lessons.objective: Attach behavior to instances of a type.
lessons.instruction: Declare increment as an instance method.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Instance methods are declared with func inside the type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: var declares a property. Use func for a method.

lessons.title: The self Property
lessons.objective: Disambiguate an instance property from a parameter.
lessons.instruction: Assign the parameter x to the stored property x.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. self refers to the current instance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Self names the conforming/current type. Use lowercase self for the instance.

lessons.title: Mutating Value Types
lessons.objective: Allow a structure method to modify its instance.
lessons.instruction: Permit moveBy to change x and y.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. mutating permits a value-type method to change self.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: static makes a type method. Use mutating for instance mutation.
lessons.sourceTitle: Methods · Modifying Value Types from Within Instance Methods

lessons.title: Assigning to self
lessons.objective: Replace an entire value-type instance inside a mutating method.
lessons.instruction: Move by replacing the current Point value.
lessons.codePrefix: mutating func moveBy(x: Double, y: Double) {
lessons.codeSuffix:
= Point(x: self.x + x, y: self.y + y)
}
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A mutating method may assign a new value to self.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Self is the type. Assign the replacement instance to lowercase self.
lessons.sourceTitle: Methods · Assigning to self Within a Mutating Method

lessons.title: Type Methods
lessons.objective: Call behavior on a type rather than an instance.
lessons.instruction: Declare a structure type method.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. static declares a type method.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: mutating applies to instance methods. Use static for type behavior.

levels.title: Level 12 · Subscripts
levels.summary: Expose indexed access on instances and types.

lessons.title: Subscript Syntax
lessons.objective: Define indexed read access.
lessons.instruction: Declare the accessor used with timesTable[index].
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. subscript defines bracket-based access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A function is called with a name. Bracket access uses subscript.

lessons.title: Subscript Usage
lessons.objective: Read a value using square brackets.
lessons.instruction: Read the sixth multiple from threeTimesTable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Subscripts are accessed with square brackets.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Parentheses call a function or initializer. Use brackets for a subscript.

lessons.title: Subscript Options
lessons.objective: Define a subscript with multiple parameters.
lessons.instruction: Read a matrix element at row two, column one.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A subscript can accept multiple comma-separated arguments.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: These are two subscript arguments, not one tuple argument.

lessons.title: Type Subscripts
lessons.objective: Provide indexed access directly on a type.
lessons.instruction: Declare a static subscript.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. static places the subscript on the type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Type subscripts use static.

levels.title: Level 13 · Inheritance
levels.summary: Specialize classes safely with subclassing and overrides.

lessons.title: Base Classes
lessons.objective: Define a class that doesn't inherit from another class.
lessons.instruction: Declare Vehicle as a base class.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A class without a superclass is a base class.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: protocol declares requirements. Use class for Vehicle.

lessons.title: Subclassing
lessons.objective: Derive a specialized class from a superclass.
lessons.instruction: Make Bicycle inherit from Vehicle.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A colon followed by the superclass establishes inheritance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Class inheritance uses : Superclass.

lessons.title: Accessing Superclass Behavior
lessons.objective: Call an overridden member's superclass implementation.
lessons.instruction: Start the overridden description with Vehicle's description.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. super accesses the superclass implementation.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: self.description would recursively access the override. Use super.description.
lessons.sourceTitle: Inheritance · Accessing Superclass Methods, Properties, and Subscripts

lessons.title: Overriding Methods
lessons.objective: Replace inherited method behavior explicitly.
lessons.instruction: Mark makeNoise as an override.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. override acknowledges replacement of an inherited declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses override, not overload, for inherited behavior.

lessons.title: Overriding Properties
lessons.objective: Override an inherited property's accessor behavior.
lessons.instruction: Mark the computed description property as inherited replacement.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. override applies to inherited properties as well as methods.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: static would create type-level storage. Use override.
lessons.sourceTitle: Inheritance · Overriding Property Getters and Setters

lessons.title: Overriding Property Observers
lessons.objective: Observe changes to an inherited property.
lessons.instruction: Run logic after AutomaticCar.currentSpeed changes.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. didSet observes the inherited stored property after mutation.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: get replaces read behavior. Use didSet to observe changes.

lessons.title: Preventing Overrides
lessons.objective: Prevent subclass replacement of a declaration.
lessons.instruction: Prevent subclasses from overriding reset().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. final prohibits overriding.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: private limits visibility. final specifically prevents overrides.

levels.title: Level 14 · Initialization
levels.summary: Establish valid initial state across value and class hierarchies.

lessons.title: Initializers
lessons.objective: Initialize every stored property before an instance is used.
lessons.instruction: Declare Fahrenheit's initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. init establishes the instance's initial state.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift initializers use init, not new.

lessons.title: Initialization Bypasses Property Observers
lessons.objective: Predict whether initialization assignments call property observers.
lessons.instruction: Choose whether a default value or initializer assignment calls didSet.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Default-value and initializer assignments set storage directly without calling property observers.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Property observers aren't called while default values or initializer assignments establish initial storage.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Initial Values and Property Observers

lessons.title: Default Property Values
lessons.objective: Provide initial storage at the declaration site.
lessons.instruction: Give temperature a default value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Assignment syntax supplies a default property value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: == compares values. Use = to initialize storage.

lessons.title: Initialization Parameters
lessons.objective: Accept caller-provided initial state.
lessons.instruction: Accept a Celsius temperature when initializing.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Initializers take typed parameters like functions.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Initializers don't declare return types. Put celsius in the parameter list.

lessons.title: Initializer Argument Labels
lessons.objective: Use a distinct external label for clarity.
lessons.instruction: Expose fromFahrenheit as the call-site label.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The external label makes calls read Temperature(fromFahrenheit:).
lessons.incorrectFeedback: _ removes the label. Use fromFahrenheit for the call site.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Parameter Names and Argument Labels

lessons.title: Parameters Without Labels
lessons.objective: Remove an initializer argument label deliberately.
lessons.instruction: Allow Color(1.0) without a label.
lessons.codeSuffix: white: Double) { red = white; green = white; blue = white }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. _ suppresses the external argument label.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use _ before the local parameter name to omit its label.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Initializer Parameters Without Argument Labels

lessons.title: Optional Initial State
lessons.objective: Represent a property whose value is initially absent.
lessons.instruction: Allow response to begin without a survey answer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Optional stored properties automatically start as nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A nonoptional String needs a value before initialization completes. Use String?.

lessons.title: Initialize Constant Properties
lessons.objective: Assign a constant stored property exactly once during initialization.
lessons.instruction: Store the supplied question in the let property.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An initializer may assign its own let property once.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The property belongs to this instance. Assign self.text.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Assigning Constant Properties During Initialization

lessons.title: Default Initializers
lessons.objective: Use a synthesized initializer when every property has a default.
lessons.instruction: Create ShoppingListItem with its default initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The type receives init() when all properties have defaults and no custom initializer blocks synthesis.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Call the synthesized initializer with parentheses.

lessons.title: Memberwise Initializer Defaults
lessons.objective: Use defaulted structure members selectively.
lessons.instruction: Create Size with only height customized.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Defaulted members can be omitted from the memberwise call.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The synthesized memberwise initializer uses the property label height:.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Memberwise Initializers for Structure Types

lessons.title: Value-Type Delegation
lessons.objective: Delegate from one value-type initializer to another.
lessons.instruction: Delegate Rect initialization to its existing initializer.
lessons.codePrefix:
init(center: Point, size: Size) {
    let origin = Point()
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Value types delegate with self.init.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Value types have no superclass. Delegate with self.init.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Initializer Delegation for Value Types

lessons.title: Convenience Initializers
lessons.objective: Declare a secondary class initializer that delegates across.
lessons.instruction: Mark this class initializer as convenience.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. convenience marks a class initializer that must delegate to another initializer in the same class.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses convenience for secondary class initializers.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Syntax for Designated and Convenience Initializers

lessons.title: Class Delegation Upward
lessons.objective: Delegate from a designated subclass initializer to its superclass.
lessons.instruction: Initialize the inherited name property through the superclass initializer.
lessons.codePrefix:
init(name: String, quantity: Int) {
    self.quantity = quantity
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A designated initializer delegates up with super.init.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: self.init delegates across the same class. Use super.init to initialize the superclass.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Initializer Delegation for Class Types

lessons.title: Two-Phase Initialization
lessons.objective: Initialize subclass storage before delegating upward.
lessons.instruction: Choose the first action in a designated subclass initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Phase one initializes all storage introduced by the subclass before super.init completes the hierarchy.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Initialize the subclass's stored properties before using the instance.

lessons.title: Overriding Initializers
lessons.objective: Acknowledge replacement of an inherited designated initializer.
lessons.instruction: Mark the inherited designated init(name:) implementation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An inherited designated initializer replacement uses override.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: required imposes a subclass requirement. Use override for this inherited declaration.

lessons.title: Automatic Initializer Inheritance
lessons.objective: Recognize when a subclass inherits superclass initializers.
lessons.instruction: Choose the subclass declaration that can inherit superclass designated initializers automatically.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Defaulting new storage helps satisfy the conditions for automatic initializer inheritance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Subclass storage must be initialized before inherited initializers can construct valid instances.

lessons.title: Failable Initializers
lessons.objective: Reject invalid initialization with nil.
lessons.instruction: Declare Animal initialization as failable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. init? returns an optional instance and can return nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The question mark belongs directly after init for a failable initializer.

lessons.title: Failable Enum Initialization
lessons.objective: Return nil when input doesn't identify an enum case.
lessons.instruction: Reject unknown temperature symbols.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A failable initializer signals failure by returning nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: No error is thrown here. Return nil from init?.

lessons.title: Raw-Value Initialization Failure
lessons.objective: Use synthesized failable raw-value initialization.
lessons.instruction: Attempt to create a TemperatureUnit from a Character.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Raw-value enums synthesize init?(rawValue:).
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use the synthesized rawValue: label.
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Failable Initializers for Enumerations with Raw Values

lessons.title: Initialization Failure Propagation
lessons.objective: Propagate failure from a delegated initializer.
lessons.instruction: Delegate to a failable Product initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Failure from super.init? automatically fails the subclass initializer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The name storage belongs to Product. Delegate upward with super.init.

lessons.title: Override Failable Initialization
lessons.objective: Replace a failable initializer with a nonfailable one when validity can be guaranteed.
lessons.instruction: Make Document's override always construct a named instance.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A subclass can override init? with nonfailable init when it guarantees success.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The requested override guarantees a fallback name, so use nonfailable init.

lessons.title: Required Initializers
lessons.objective: Require every subclass to implement or inherit an initializer.
lessons.instruction: Mark the initializer as mandatory throughout the hierarchy.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. required propagates the initializer requirement to subclasses.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Initializers aren't marked final. Use required for a hierarchy-wide requirement.

lessons.title: Closure-Computed Defaults
lessons.objective: Compute a default property value once during initialization.
lessons.instruction: Execute the closure that builds the board array.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The trailing () executes the closure and stores its returned array.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Without (), the value is the closure itself. Invoke it to produce [Bool].
lessons.sourceTitle: Initialization · Setting a Default Property Value with a Closure or Function

levels.title: Level 15 · Deinitialization
levels.summary: Release class-owned resources when an instance leaves memory.

lessons.title: Deinitializer Syntax
lessons.objective: Run cleanup immediately before a class instance is deallocated.
lessons.instruction: Declare Banker's cleanup block.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. deinit declares a parameterless class deinitializer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses deinit, not destroy.

lessons.title: Cleanup on Release
lessons.objective: Let ARC trigger cleanup when the last strong reference disappears.
lessons.instruction: Release the optional's strong reference to the player.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Assigning nil removes this strong reference; deinit runs if no others remain.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Creating another Player doesn't express release. Assign nil to the optional reference.

levels.title: Level 16 · Optional Chaining
levels.summary: Access nested optional state without forced unwrapping.

lessons.title: Safe Chaining
lessons.objective: Access a member only when the optional base contains a value.
lessons.instruction: Read residence room count without forcing person.residence.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ?. returns nil instead of trapping when residence is nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: ! traps when residence is nil. Use optional chaining with ?.
lessons.sourceTitle: Optional Chaining · Alternative to Forced Unwrapping

lessons.title: Optional Relationships
lessons.objective: Model a relationship that can be absent.
lessons.instruction: Allow a Person to have no Residence yet.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Residence? represents either a residence or nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The relationship must represent absence. Use Residence?.

lessons.title: Assign Through a Chain
lessons.objective: Assign only when the optional path exists.
lessons.instruction: Attempt to assign an address through optional residence.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The assignment succeeds only when residence is non-nil.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Forced unwrapping can trap. Use ? for conditional assignment.

lessons.title: Call Methods Through a Chain
lessons.objective: Observe whether an optional-chained Void method ran.
lessons.instruction: Call printNumberOfRooms only when residence exists.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The chained Void call has type Void? and is nil when skipped.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use ? to skip the call safely when residence is absent.

lessons.title: Subscripts Through a Chain
lessons.objective: Index only when the optional base exists.
lessons.instruction: Read the first room safely.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The question mark appears before the subscript brackets.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use residence?[0] for an optional-chained subscript.

lessons.title: Optional Subscript Results
lessons.objective: Continue chaining from an optional value returned by a subscript.
lessons.instruction: Read the name from the first optional room.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ? after the brackets chains from the optional subscript result.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The subscript itself returns an optional. Chain from it with ?.
lessons.sourceTitle: Optional Chaining · Accessing Subscripts of Optional Type

lessons.title: Multiple Chaining Levels
lessons.objective: Traverse several optional relationships in one expression.
lessons.instruction: Safely read the building identifier through residence and address.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Each optional link uses ?; the result stays optional without adding nested optionals.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Address can also be nil. Continue with another optional chain.

lessons.title: Chain Optional Returns
lessons.objective: Continue from a method that itself returns an optional.
lessons.instruction: Uppercase an optional building identifier safely.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The method's optional return value can be chained again.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: buildingIdentifier() may return nil. Chain with ? before uppercased().
lessons.sourceTitle: Optional Chaining · Methods with Optional Return Values

levels.title: Level 17 · Error Handling
levels.summary: Throw, propagate, catch, type, and clean up recoverable failures.

lessons.title: NSError Interoperability
lessons.objective: Recognize Swift error interoperability with Cocoa NSError patterns.
lessons.instruction: Choose the Cocoa error type that interoperates with Swift error handling.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Swift error handling interoperates with Cocoa patterns based on NSError.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: NSException is an exception class. Swift errors interoperate with NSError patterns.

lessons.title: Throwing Without Stack Unwinding
lessons.objective: Distinguish Swift throwing from exception mechanisms that unwind the call stack.
lessons.instruction: Choose whether Swift throw uses exception-style stack unwinding.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Swift error handling doesn't use exception-style stack unwinding.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift throw resembles exception syntax, but Swift error handling doesn't unwind the call stack like those exception mechanisms.
lessons.sourceTitle: Error Handling · Throwing and Stack Unwinding

lessons.title: Representing and Throwing Errors
lessons.objective: Throw a typed error value when an operation can't continue.
lessons.instruction: Signal that the vending machine lacks inventory.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. throw transfers control with an Error value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Returning an error value doesn't activate Swift error propagation. Use throw.
lessons.sourceTitle: Error Handling · Representing and Throwing Errors

lessons.title: Handling with do-catch
lessons.objective: Handle a thrown error with matching catch clauses.
lessons.instruction: Start the protected scope around a throwing call.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. do introduces the scope whose errors are handled by catch.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: try marks the throwing expression. The surrounding handler begins with do.
lessons.sourceTitle: Error Handling · Handling Errors Using Do-Catch

lessons.title: Convert Errors to Optionals
lessons.objective: Turn a throwing expression into an optional result.
lessons.instruction: Return nil when fetchData() throws.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. try? produces nil when an error is thrown.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: try! traps on an error. Use try? to convert failure to nil.
lessons.sourceTitle: Error Handling · Converting Errors to Optional Values

lessons.title: Disable Error Propagation
lessons.objective: Assert that a throwing expression cannot fail.
lessons.instruction: Load a bundled resource whose validity is guaranteed.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. try! produces a nonoptional result but traps if the guarantee is wrong.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: try? hides failure as nil. The explicit no-failure assertion is try!.

lessons.title: Typed Throws
lessons.objective: Constrain a function to one declared error type.
lessons.instruction: Declare that summarize can throw only StatisticsError.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. throws(StatisticsError) specifies the concrete propagated error type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The requirement is the concrete StatisticsError type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Error Handling · Specifying the Error Type

lessons.title: Cleanup Actions
lessons.objective: Run cleanup whenever the current scope exits.
lessons.instruction: Ensure close(file) runs after processing regardless of exit path.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. defer executes when the surrounding scope exits.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: catch runs only for handled errors. defer covers every scope exit.

levels.title: Level 18 · Concurrency
levels.summary: Coordinate asynchronous work with tasks, isolation, actors, and Sendable data.

lessons.title: Async Thread Independence
lessons.objective: Recognize that an async function isn't bound to one thread across suspension.
lessons.instruction: Choose whether an async function must resume on the same thread where it suspended.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An async function can suspend on one thread and resume on another.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift concurrency doesn't guarantee that an async function resumes on its original thread.

lessons.title: Asynchronous Functions
lessons.objective: Declare and call work that can suspend.
lessons.instruction: Mark listPhotos as asynchronous.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. async belongs in the function declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: await marks a potentially suspending call. Declarations use async.
lessons.sourceTitle: Concurrency · Defining and Calling Asynchronous Functions

lessons.title: Await Suspension
lessons.objective: Mark a call that may suspend the current task.
lessons.instruction: Call listPhotos from asynchronous context.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. await marks the potential suspension point.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: async declares asynchronous functions. Calls use await.
lessons.sourceTitle: Concurrency · Defining and Calling Asynchronous Functions

lessons.title: Asynchronous Sequences
lessons.objective: Iterate values that arrive asynchronously.
lessons.instruction: Await each value from an AsyncSequence.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. for try await handles asynchronous iteration that can throw.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: This sequence is asynchronous and throwing. Use for try await.

lessons.title: Parallel Child Tasks
lessons.objective: Start independent asynchronous work before awaiting results.
lessons.instruction: Begin downloading the first photo concurrently.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. async let creates a child task immediately.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Declare concurrent child work with async let, then await its value later.
lessons.sourceTitle: Concurrency · Calling Asynchronous Functions in Parallel

lessons.title: Task Groups
lessons.objective: Create a dynamic group of structured child tasks.
lessons.instruction: Start a throwing task group that returns Photos.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. withThrowingTaskGroup scopes child tasks and their lifetime.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Task.detached creates unstructured work. Use a throwing task group for structured children.

lessons.title: Task Cancellation
lessons.objective: Cooperatively stop work after cancellation is requested.
lessons.instruction: Throw CancellationError when the current task is cancelled.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Task.checkCancellation() throws when cancellation has been requested.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Cancellation is checked cooperatively with Task.checkCancellation().

lessons.title: Unstructured Tasks
lessons.objective: Create a task outside a structured child-task scope.
lessons.instruction: Launch work that inherits the current actor and task-local context.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Task { } creates unstructured work while inheriting current context.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Task.detached doesn't inherit actor context. Use Task { } here.

lessons.title: Isolation
lessons.objective: Keep mutable state inside an isolation domain.
lessons.instruction: Choose the construct that serializes access to mutable balance.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An actor protects its isolated mutable state from concurrent access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A struct has value semantics but doesn't itself establish actor isolation.

lessons.title: The Main Actor
lessons.objective: Isolate UI-observed state to the main actor.
lessons.instruction: Constrain this view model to the main actor.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @MainActor isolates the declaration to the main actor.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @Sendable constrains closures. UI state isolation uses @MainActor.

lessons.title: Actors
lessons.objective: Access actor-isolated state across an asynchronous boundary.
lessons.instruction: Read the actor's balance from outside its isolation domain.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Cross-actor access can suspend and requires await.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Actor isolation creates an async boundary, not necessarily a throwing one. Use await.

lessons.title: Global Actors
lessons.objective: Share one actor isolation domain across declarations.
lessons.instruction: Declare UIActor as a global actor.
lessons.codeSuffix: actor UIActor { static let shared = UIActor() }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @globalActor defines a custom global actor type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @MainActor applies an existing global actor. Define one with @globalActor.

lessons.title: Sendable Types
lessons.objective: Mark data safe to transfer across isolation domains.
lessons.instruction: Declare TemperatureReading as transferable concurrent data.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Sendable expresses safe transfer across concurrency domains.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Actor is a reference-type isolation model. Transferable value data conforms to Sendable.

levels.title: Level 19 · Macros
levels.summary: Generate checked Swift source during compilation.

lessons.title: Freestanding Macros
lessons.objective: Invoke a freestanding macro with number-sign syntax.
lessons.instruction: Expand a source-location expression.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Freestanding macro invocations begin with #.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @ applies attached macros to declarations. Freestanding macros use #.

lessons.title: Attached Macros
lessons.objective: Attach compile-time behavior to a declaration.
lessons.instruction: Apply the OptionSet macro to SundaeToppings.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Attached macros use attribute syntax beginning with @.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: # invokes a freestanding macro. Apply an attached macro with @.

lessons.title: Macro Declarations
lessons.objective: Declare a macro's public signature.
lessons.instruction: Declare stringify as a freestanding expression macro.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. macro declares the interface exposed to callers.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A macro declaration uses macro, not func.

lessons.title: External Macro Implementations
lessons.objective: Connect a macro declaration to its compiler plug-in type.
lessons.instruction: Name the external module and implementation type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #externalMacro identifies the plug-in module and implementation type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The declaration must name its implementation module and type.

lessons.title: Macro Expansion
lessons.objective: Recognize macro output as compile-time Swift source.
lessons.instruction: Choose when the compiler expands a macro.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The compiler expands macros before compiling the resulting source.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Macros transform source during compilation, not at runtime.

lessons.title: Implementing Expression Macros
lessons.objective: Implement a freestanding expression macro role.
lessons.instruction: Conform StringifyMacro to the matching macro protocol.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A freestanding expression macro implementation conforms to ExpressionMacro.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: MemberMacro implements an attached member role. Use ExpressionMacro.

lessons.title: Testing Macro Expansion
lessons.objective: Verify generated source independently of runtime behavior.
lessons.instruction: Choose the testing focus for a macro implementation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Macro tests compare produced syntax and diagnostics.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Macro implementation is compile-time source transformation; test its expansion and diagnostics.

levels.title: Level 20 · Type Casting
levels.summary: Inspect and safely recover concrete runtime types.

lessons.title: Casting Class Hierarchies
lessons.objective: Store related subclass instances behind a superclass type.
lessons.instruction: Declare a library that can contain Movie and Song values.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The shared MediaItem superclass can hold both subclasses.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A Movie array can't contain Song. Use their common superclass.
lessons.sourceTitle: Type Casting · Defining a Class Hierarchy

lessons.title: Checking Type
lessons.objective: Check a value's runtime type without changing it.
lessons.instruction: Count items whose runtime type is Movie.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. is returns whether a value has the tested runtime type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: as performs a cast. Use is for a Boolean type check.

lessons.title: Conditional Downcasting
lessons.objective: Attempt a downcast without trapping.
lessons.instruction: Enter the branch only when item is a Movie.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. as? returns an optional and supports safe conditional binding.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: as! traps when the runtime type doesn't match. Use as?.

lessons.title: Any Values
lessons.objective: Store values of arbitrary types in a heterogeneous collection.
lessons.instruction: Choose the type that can represent values of any Swift type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Any can represent instances of any type, including value types.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: AnyObject represents class instances only. Use Any for mixed value and reference types.

levels.title: Level 21 · Nested Types
levels.summary: Scope supporting types inside the type they serve.

lessons.title: Nested Types in Action
lessons.objective: Declare a supporting enumeration inside a structure.
lessons.instruction: Nest Suit inside BlackjackCard.
lessons.codeSuffix:
Suit { case spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs }
}
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Types can be declared inside another type's scope.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: extension adds members to an existing type. Declare the nested type with enum.

lessons.title: Referring to Nested Types
lessons.objective: Qualify a nested type with its containing type.
lessons.instruction: Refer to the nested Hearts suit.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Nested types are referenced through their containing type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Suit is nested inside BlackjackCard. Qualify both names.
lessons.sourceTitle: Nested Types · Referring to Nested Types

levels.title: Level 22 · Extensions
levels.summary: Add focused capabilities to existing types.

lessons.title: Extensions Don't Override
lessons.objective: Distinguish adding extension functionality from overriding existing functionality.
lessons.instruction: Choose the capability an extension provides.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extensions add new functionality but can't override existing functionality.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Extensions can't override existing functionality; they add new capabilities to an existing type.

lessons.title: Extension Syntax
lessons.objective: Add functionality to an existing type.
lessons.instruction: Open an extension on Double.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. extension adds capabilities without subclassing.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use extension to add members to an existing type.

lessons.title: Extension Computed Properties
lessons.objective: Add a derived property without adding storage.
lessons.instruction: Convert kilometers to meters in a Double extension.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extensions can add computed properties.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Extensions can't add stored instance properties. Return a computed expression.

lessons.title: Extension Initializers
lessons.objective: Add a convenience initializer while preserving existing initialization.
lessons.instruction: Add a size-based Rect initializer in an extension.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extensions can add initializers under the type's initialization rules.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift initialization uses init.

lessons.title: Extension Methods
lessons.objective: Add an instance method to an existing type.
lessons.instruction: Add repetitions(of:) to Int.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extensions can add instance and type methods.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A callable method is declared with func.

lessons.title: Mutating Extension Methods
lessons.objective: Modify a value-type instance from an extension method.
lessons.instruction: Allow Int.square() to replace self.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A value-type extension method must be mutating to assign self.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: static creates a type method. Use mutating for instance replacement.

lessons.title: Extension Subscripts
lessons.objective: Add indexed access to an existing type.
lessons.instruction: Declare an Int digit subscript.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extensions can add subscripts.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Bracket access is declared with subscript.

lessons.title: Nested Types in Extensions
lessons.objective: Add a nested type to an existing type.
lessons.instruction: Add Kind inside Int's extension.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An extension can introduce a nested type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: case belongs inside an enum. Declare Kind with enum.

levels.title: Level 23 · Protocols
levels.summary: Define contracts, compose capabilities, and share default behavior.

lessons.title: Protocol Syntax
lessons.objective: Declare a named set of requirements.
lessons.instruction: Declare FullyNamed as a protocol.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. protocol declares requirements that conforming types satisfy.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use protocol for a conformance contract.

lessons.title: Property Requirements
lessons.objective: Require readable and writable property behavior without choosing storage.
lessons.instruction: Require mustBeSettable to support reads and writes.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Protocol property requirements specify get and optionally set access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Protocols don't require stored versus computed implementation. Use get set.

lessons.title: Method Requirements
lessons.objective: Require an instance method signature without a body.
lessons.instruction: Require random() to return Double.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Protocol method requirements use normal func signatures without bodies.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use func for a required method.

lessons.title: Mutating Requirements
lessons.objective: Permit conforming value types to mutate themselves.
lessons.instruction: Require toggle() to modify conforming value types.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. mutating lets value-type conformances change self.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: static requires type behavior. Instance mutation uses mutating.

lessons.title: Initializer Requirements
lessons.objective: Require conforming types to provide an initializer.
lessons.instruction: Require init(someParameter:).
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Initializer requirements use init without a body.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: init is its own declaration; don't prefix it with func.

lessons.title: Class Initializer Conformance
lessons.objective: Preserve an initializer requirement for all subclasses.
lessons.instruction: Implement a protocol-required initializer in a nonfinal class.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. required ensures subclasses also satisfy the protocol initializer requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A protocol requirement isn't necessarily a superclass override. Use required.
lessons.sourceTitle: Protocols · Class Implementations of Initializer Requirements

lessons.title: Failable Initializer Requirements
lessons.objective: Require initialization that can fail.
lessons.instruction: Declare a failable protocol initializer.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. init? declares a failable initializer requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Failability is written as ? directly after init.

lessons.title: Semantic Requirements
lessons.objective: Adopt a protocol whose requirements describe behavior rather than members.
lessons.instruction: Mark transferable value data for concurrency domains.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Sendable expresses semantic safety across concurrency domains.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Actor is an isolation model. Transferable data adopts Sendable.

lessons.title: Protocols as Types
lessons.objective: Store a value of any concrete type conforming to a protocol.
lessons.instruction: Declare generator as a boxed protocol value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. any creates a boxed existential that can hold any conforming concrete type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: some hides one fixed concrete type. A stored existential uses any.

lessons.title: Delegation
lessons.objective: Hand responsibility to an injected protocol-conforming object.
lessons.instruction: Keep a delegate reference without creating a strong cycle.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A class-only delegate can be weak to avoid retaining its owner cycle.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift has no strong modifier, and a strong delegate can form a cycle. Use weak.

lessons.title: Conformance in an Extension
lessons.objective: Add protocol adoption separately from a type's original declaration.
lessons.instruction: Make Dice conform to TextRepresentable in an extension.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An extension lists adopted protocols after a colon.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Conformance names the protocol directly; any is for existential values.
lessons.sourceTitle: Protocols · Adding Conformance with an Extension

lessons.title: Conditional Conformance
lessons.objective: Conform a generic type only when its element satisfies a constraint.
lessons.instruction: Conform Array when Element is TextRepresentable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A where clause constrains conditional conformance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic constraints use where, not if.

lessons.title: Declare Adoption Explicitly
lessons.objective: State conformance even when requirements already happen to exist.
lessons.instruction: Declare Hamster's TextRepresentable adoption.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Existing matching members don't imply conformance; declare it with : Protocol.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Protocol adoption uses a colon.
lessons.sourceTitle: Protocols · Declaring Adoption with an Extension

lessons.title: Synthesized Conformance
lessons.objective: Request compiler-generated equality for eligible stored properties.
lessons.instruction: Make Vector3D comparable with ==.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Equatable can be synthesized when every stored property is Equatable.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Comparable additionally requires ordering. Use Equatable for ==.

lessons.title: Implicit Conformance
lessons.objective: Recognize compiler-inferred semantic conformance.
lessons.instruction: Choose the protocol commonly inferred for safe value data crossing concurrency boundaries.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Swift can infer Sendable for eligible types under its conformance rules.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: AnyObject is a class constraint, not an inferred transfer-safety conformance.

lessons.title: Collections of Protocol Types
lessons.objective: Store heterogeneous conforming values together.
lessons.instruction: Declare an array containing different TextRepresentable types.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An existential collection can hold different conforming concrete types.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: some requires one fixed hidden type. Heterogeneous storage uses any.

lessons.title: Protocol Inheritance
lessons.objective: Refine one protocol with another protocol's requirements.
lessons.instruction: Make PrettyTextRepresentable inherit TextRepresentable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Protocol inheritance lists the refined protocol directly.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: any denotes a value type. Inherit requirements from TextRepresentable directly.

lessons.title: Class-Only Protocols
lessons.objective: Restrict protocol adoption to class types.
lessons.instruction: Make SomeClassOnlyProtocol class-only.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Inheriting AnyObject restricts conformance to classes.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Any includes value types. Use AnyObject for class-only adoption.

lessons.title: Protocol Composition
lessons.objective: Require a value to conform to multiple protocols simultaneously.
lessons.instruction: Accept values that are both Named and Aged.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. & composes multiple protocol requirements.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift protocol composition uses &.

lessons.title: Checking Protocol Conformance
lessons.objective: Safely cast a runtime value to a protocol existential.
lessons.instruction: Enter the branch only when object conforms to HasArea.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. as? both checks conformance and returns an optional protocol value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: is returns only Bool. Use as? to bind the conforming value.

lessons.title: Optional Protocol Requirements
lessons.objective: Call an Objective-C-compatible optional requirement safely.
lessons.instruction: Call increment only if the data source and optional method exist.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Optional chaining handles both the optional delegate and optional requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Forced unwrapping can trap when the delegate is absent. Use ?.

lessons.title: Protocol Extensions
lessons.objective: Add behavior available to all conforming types.
lessons.instruction: Extend RandomNumberGenerator with randomBool().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Extend the protocol declaration itself.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: any RandomNumberGenerator is an existential type. Extend the protocol name.

lessons.title: Default Implementations
lessons.objective: Provide shared behavior satisfying a protocol requirement.
lessons.instruction: Provide a default textualDescription implementation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A protocol extension can provide a computed property implementation.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Computed properties use var.

lessons.title: Constrained Protocol Extensions
lessons.objective: Offer default behavior only to conformers meeting extra constraints.
lessons.instruction: Limit prettyText to collection-like conformers.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. where constrains which conformers receive extension members.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic constraints are expressed with where.
lessons.sourceTitle: Protocols · Adding Constraints to Protocol Extensions

levels.title: Level 24 · Generics
levels.summary: Write reusable algorithms and containers with precise type relationships.

lessons.title: The Generic Problem
lessons.objective: Replace repeated type-specific algorithms with one abstraction.
lessons.instruction: Choose the capability shared by Int and String swap implementations.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A generic function removes type-specific duplication while preserving type safety.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: One function per type repeats the same algorithm. Use a generic abstraction.

lessons.title: Generic Functions
lessons.objective: Parameterize a function over a placeholder type.
lessons.instruction: Declare swapTwoValues over type T.
lessons.codeSuffix: (_ a: inout T, _ b: inout T) { swap(&a, &b) }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. <T> introduces a type parameter used by the signature.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic parameters are declared directly as <T>.

lessons.title: Type Parameters
