lessons.objective: Use one placeholder consistently across parameters.
lessons.instruction: Require both swap arguments to have the same generic type.
lessons.codePrefix: func swapTwoValues<T>(_ a: inout T, _ b: inout
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Reusing T requires both arguments to share one concrete type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Any erases the same-type relationship. Reuse T.

lessons.title: Generic Types
lessons.objective: Store elements of a caller-selected type.
lessons.instruction: Parameterize Stack over Element.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Element is the generic type parameter for each Stack specialization.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Declare the placeholder directly as <Element>.

lessons.title: Extending Generic Types
lessons.objective: Use an existing generic parameter inside an extension without redeclaring it.
lessons.instruction: Return the top Stack element when present.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The original Element parameter remains available in the extension.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: No T is declared here. Use Stack's existing Element name.

lessons.title: Type Constraint Syntax
lessons.objective: Require a generic parameter to conform to a protocol.
lessons.instruction: Require T to conform to Equatable.
lessons.codeSuffix: >(of value: T, in array: [T]) -> Int? { nil }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A colon adds a conformance constraint to a type parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic conformance constraints use : Protocol.

lessons.title: Constraints in Action
lessons.objective: Use operations guaranteed by a generic constraint.
lessons.instruction: Compare an element with the Equatable target.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Equatable guarantees == for values of T.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: === checks class identity. The Equatable constraint enables ==.

lessons.title: Associated Types
lessons.objective: Give a protocol a placeholder type chosen by each conformance.
lessons.instruction: Declare Container's item placeholder.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. associatedtype declares a protocol placeholder resolved by each conformer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: typealias names an already known type. Protocol placeholders use associatedtype.

lessons.title: Infer an Associated Type
lessons.objective: Let a conformance infer its associated type from existing members.
lessons.instruction: Conform Array to Container without restating Element.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Existing Array members allow Swift to infer Item as Element.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: This protocol conformance is declared as Container; matching members infer the associated type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Generics · Extending Existing Types for Associated Types

lessons.title: Constrained Associated Types
lessons.objective: Require every associated type choice to meet a protocol constraint.
lessons.instruction: Require Container.Item to be Equatable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The associated type must satisfy Equatable.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Any adds no equality guarantee. Constrain Item to Equatable.
lessons.sourceTitle: Generics · Adding Constraints to an Associated Type

lessons.title: Protocol in Associated Constraints
lessons.objective: Relate an associated type to another protocol's associated type.
lessons.instruction: Require Suffix.Item to equal Container.Item.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. == expresses a same-type requirement between associated types.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A colon expresses conformance. Use == for identical associated types.
lessons.sourceTitle: Generics · Protocols in Associated Type Constraints

lessons.title: Generic Where Clauses
lessons.objective: Express relationships among generic and associated types.
lessons.instruction: Require two containers to hold the same Item type.
lessons.codePrefix: func allItemsMatch<C1: Container, C2: Container>(_ c1: C1, _ c2: C2) -> Bool where C1.Item
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A generic where clause uses == for a same-type requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic same-type constraints use ==.

lessons.title: Extensions with Where Clauses
lessons.objective: Expose members only for qualifying generic specializations.
lessons.instruction: Add isTop only when Stack.Element is Equatable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. where limits the extension to matching specializations.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Generic extension constraints use where.
lessons.sourceTitle: Generics · Extensions with a Generic Where Clause

lessons.title: Contextual Where Clauses
lessons.objective: Constrain an individual generic member near its declaration.
lessons.instruction: Make average available only for Int elements.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A contextual where clause constrains this member.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: guard is runtime control flow. Use a compile-time where constraint.

lessons.title: Associated Types with Where
lessons.objective: Constrain an associated iterator's element relationship.
lessons.instruction: Require Iterator.Element to equal Item.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The iterator and container expose the same element type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use == for a same-type relationship.
lessons.sourceTitle: Generics · Associated Types with a Generic Where Clause

lessons.title: Generic Subscripts
lessons.objective: Give a subscript its own generic sequence parameter.
lessons.instruction: Declare indices as any Sequence.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The generic subscript accepts any Sequence satisfying its where clause.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Array<Int> is one concrete type. Constrain the parameter to Sequence.

lessons.title: Implicit Generic Constraints
lessons.objective: Suppress the usual Copyable requirement when generic code accepts noncopyable values.
lessons.instruction: Allow T to be either copyable or noncopyable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ~Copyable suppresses the implicit Copyable constraint.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Copyable requires copying support. Prefix it with ~ to allow either ownership model.

levels.title: Level 25 · Opaque and Boxed Protocol Types
levels.summary: Choose hidden concrete results or type-erased heterogeneous storage.

lessons.title: The Opaque-Type Problem
lessons.objective: Hide implementation detail without losing concrete type identity.
lessons.instruction: Choose the return model that preserves one hidden Shape type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An opaque result hides its concrete name while preserving one underlying type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A boxed existential can hold varying conforming types. The requirement is one hidden concrete type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Opaque Types · The Problem Opaque Types Solve

lessons.title: Returning an Opaque Type
lessons.objective: Return one hidden concrete conformer.
lessons.instruction: Hide the concrete Shape returned by makeTrapezoid().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. some Shape exposes conformance while hiding one concrete result type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: any boxes an arbitrary conformer. Use some for an opaque result.
lessons.sourceTitle: Opaque Types · Returning an Opaque Type

lessons.title: Boxed Protocol Types
lessons.objective: Store any conforming concrete value behind one existential type.
lessons.instruction: Accept a Shape value whose concrete type may vary at runtime.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. any Shape is a boxed protocol type that can hold different conformers.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: some requires one fixed hidden concrete type. Use any for existential storage.

lessons.title: Opaque vs Boxed Identity
lessons.objective: Preserve same-type relationships through opaque returns.
lessons.instruction: Choose the keyword when callers must know two results share one hidden type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. some preserves the underlying type identity across calls to that declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: any erases concrete type identity. Use some.
lessons.sourceTitle: Opaque Types · Differences Between Opaque and Boxed Types

lessons.title: Opaque Parameter Types
lessons.objective: Use concise generic parameter syntax.
lessons.instruction: Accept one value of an inferred concrete Shape type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A some parameter is syntactic sugar for a constrained generic parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: any accepts a boxed existential. Use some for generic-style opaque parameter syntax.

levels.title: Level 26 · Automatic Reference Counting
levels.summary: Manage class lifetimes and break strong reference cycles.

lessons.title: How ARC Works
lessons.objective: Recognize the lifetime rule for class instances.
lessons.instruction: Choose when ARC deallocates an instance.

choices.code: "after its last strong reference is removed"

lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ARC keeps an instance alive while at least one strong reference remains.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Leaving one scope isn't sufficient if other strong references remain.

lessons.title: ARC in Action
lessons.objective: Create and remove strong references deliberately.
lessons.instruction: Remove reference3's ownership of Person.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Assigning nil removes that optional strong reference.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Creating a new instance replaces rather than simply removes ownership. Assign nil.

lessons.title: Strong Reference Cycles
lessons.objective: Identify mutual ownership that prevents deallocation.
lessons.instruction: Choose the relationship that creates a cycle between Person and Apartment.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Mutual strong references keep both instances alive.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A weak edge doesn't retain its target and breaks the cycle.
lessons.sourceTitle: ARC · Strong Reference Cycles Between Instances

lessons.title: Weak References
lessons.objective: Break a cycle when the referenced value may become nil.
lessons.instruction: Declare Apartment.tenant without retaining the Person.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. weak references are optional and become nil automatically after deallocation.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use weak when the reference may be absent during its lifetime.

lessons.title: Unowned References
lessons.objective: Break a cycle when the referenced instance must outlive the holder.
lessons.instruction: Store CreditCard.customer without retaining it.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. unowned models a nonoptional reference expected to remain alive while used.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: weak must be optional. Use unowned for this required lifetime relationship.

lessons.title: Unowned Optional References
lessons.objective: Model a nonretaining relationship that can be nil.
lessons.instruction: Declare an optional unowned department course reference.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An unowned optional doesn't retain its instance and must still obey its lifetime guarantee.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift has no strong modifier. Use unowned on the optional relationship.

lessons.title: Unowned and Implicitly Unwrapped Properties
lessons.objective: Initialize two nonoptional relationships in two phases without a cycle.
lessons.instruction: Declare Country.capitalCity for assignment during initialization.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. An implicitly unwrapped optional can start nil yet be used as nonoptional after initialization.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The model expects nonoptional use after initialization. Use City! with the paired unowned reference.
lessons.sourceTitle: ARC · Unowned References and Implicitly Unwrapped Properties

lessons.title: Strong Cycles in Closures
lessons.objective: Recognize a closure retaining its owning instance.
lessons.instruction: Identify the capture that can cycle with a stored closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A stored closure that strongly captures self can form a two-way strong cycle.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An independent value doesn't retain the closure's owner. Captured self can.
lessons.sourceTitle: ARC · Strong Reference Cycles for Closures

lessons.title: Capture Lists
lessons.objective: Choose nonstrong capture semantics for closure references.
lessons.instruction: Capture self weakly in the closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. [weak self] prevents the closure from retaining its owner.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Capturing self without weak or unowned is strong by default.

lessons.title: Weak vs Unowned Captures
lessons.objective: Choose capture ownership from the lifetime relationship.
lessons.instruction: Choose the capture when self may be deallocated before the closure runs.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. weak becomes nil safely if self is released first.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: unowned assumes self is still alive and traps if that guarantee is violated.

levels.title: Level 27 · Memory Safety
levels.summary: Prevent overlapping mutable access to the same memory.

lessons.title: Conflicting Memory Access
lessons.objective: Recognize overlapping accesses where at least one is a write.
lessons.instruction: Choose the unsafe overlap.

choices.code: "simultaneous read and write to the same storage"

lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Overlapping access conflicts when locations overlap and at least one access writes.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Independent storage doesn't conflict. The same storage with a write does.

lessons.title: Access Characteristics
lessons.objective: Reason about whether an access is read or write, long-term or instantaneous, and overlapping.
lessons.instruction: Classify passing a variable as inout.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. inout holds write access for the duration of the call.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An in-out argument reserves long-term write access until the function returns.
lessons.sourceTitle: Memory Safety · Characteristics of Memory Access

lessons.title: Conflicting inout Arguments
lessons.objective: Avoid passing the same storage to two in-out parameters.
lessons.instruction: Choose a safe call to balance(_:_:).
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Distinct variables don't overlap during the two write accesses.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Passing &a twice creates overlapping in-out write access.
lessons.sourceTitle: Memory Safety · Conflicting Access to In-Out Parameters

lessons.title: Conflicting Access to self
lessons.objective: Avoid borrowing an instance and one of its properties mutably at the same time.
lessons.instruction: Copy health before passing the player as inout.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Separate temporary storage prevents overlapping access to player and player.health.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Mutating player and player.health simultaneously overlaps the same storage.
lessons.sourceTitle: Memory Safety · Conflicting Access to self in Methods

lessons.title: Conflicting Property Access
lessons.objective: Use disjoint stored properties only when exclusivity can be proven.
lessons.instruction: Choose the universally safe swap for a global structure value.

choices.code: let h = player.health; player.health = player.energy; player.energy = h

lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Sequential access avoids an overlapping in-out exclusivity conflict.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: For a global structure, simultaneous in-out access to two properties can conflict. Use sequential accesses.
lessons.sourceTitle: Memory Safety · Conflicting Access to Properties

levels.title: Level 28 · Access Control
levels.summary: Expose only the declarations each client is allowed to use.

lessons.title: Modules, Files, and Packages
lessons.objective: Reason about the boundaries access levels protect.
lessons.instruction: Choose Swift's basic unit of code distribution for access control.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A module is one unit of code distribution imported by another module.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Classes are declarations inside modules. The distribution boundary is a module.
lessons.sourceTitle: Access Control · Modules, Files, and Packages

lessons.title: Access Levels
lessons.objective: Distinguish Swift's declaration visibility levels.
lessons.instruction: Choose the most permissive level that also allows subclassing outside the defining module.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. open permits external access, subclassing, and overriding.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: public permits external use but not external subclassing or overriding. Use open.

lessons.title: Guiding Principle
lessons.objective: Keep a declaration from exposing less-accessible types.
lessons.instruction: Choose the valid visibility for a property whose type is internal.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A declaration can't be more accessible than types used in its signature.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A public property would expose an internal type. Limit the property to internal.

lessons.title: Default Access
lessons.objective: Recognize the access level used when no modifier is written.
lessons.instruction: Choose the default access for most declarations.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Declarations are internal by default unless context applies a stricter rule.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift's normal default is internal, not private.

lessons.title: Single-Target Apps
lessons.objective: Use internal access for code shared throughout one app module.
lessons.instruction: Choose the normal access for app-internal feature types.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Internal access is normally sufficient inside one app target.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: open is for external subclassing across modules. App-internal types normally remain internal.

lessons.title: Framework APIs
lessons.objective: Expose intended API while hiding implementation detail.
lessons.instruction: Expose a framework function to importing modules.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. public exposes the declaration to importing modules.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: internal is visible only within the framework module.

lessons.title: Unit-Test Access
lessons.objective: Import an app module with internal declarations visible to tests.
lessons.instruction: Enable internal access from the test target.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @testable import exposes eligible internal declarations to the test module.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @available controls platform availability. Tests use @testable import.

lessons.title: Access-Control Syntax
lessons.objective: Apply an access modifier to a declaration.
lessons.instruction: Limit helper() to its enclosing declaration and same-file extensions.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. private limits access to the enclosing declaration and same-file extensions.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: fileprivate exposes the declaration throughout the source file. Use private for the tighter boundary.

lessons.title: Custom-Type Access
lessons.objective: Derive member defaults from a type's explicit access.
lessons.instruction: Choose the default access of a member inside a private type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Members of a private type default to private.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The enclosing private type imposes the stricter default.

lessons.title: Tuple Access
lessons.objective: Determine tuple visibility from all element types.
lessons.instruction: Choose the access of a tuple containing public and private element types.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A tuple's access is the most restrictive access among its elements.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The private element prevents the tuple type from being public.

lessons.title: Function-Type Access
lessons.objective: Limit a function to the least-accessible parameter or return type.
lessons.instruction: Choose the maximum access for a function returning a private type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A function can't expose a less-accessible return type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A private return type can't appear in a public signature.

lessons.title: Enumeration Access
lessons.objective: Recognize that enum cases share their enum's access level.
lessons.instruction: Choose the access of a case in an internal enum.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Individual cases automatically receive the enum's access level.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Cases can't be more accessible than their enum.

lessons.title: Nested-Type Access
lessons.objective: Derive a nested type's default from its container.
lessons.instruction: Choose the default access of a nested type inside a public type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Nested types inside public types remain internal unless explicitly made public.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Public doesn't automatically propagate to nested types. Their default is internal.

lessons.title: Subclass Access
lessons.objective: Keep overrides compatible with superclass visibility.
lessons.instruction: Mark a class externally subclassable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. External modules can subclass an open class.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A public class is usable externally but not subclassable there. Use open.

lessons.title: Restricted Setters
lessons.objective: Expose reads more widely than writes.
lessons.instruction: Allow public reads but only private mutation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. private(set) narrows only setter access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift supports restricted setter access with private(set).

lessons.title: Initializer Access
lessons.objective: Limit construction consistently with the initialized type.
lessons.instruction: Expose initialization of a public type to importing modules.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A public type's initializer must also be public for external construction.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An internal initializer can't be called from importing modules.

lessons.title: Protocol Access
lessons.objective: Keep requirements and conformances within valid visibility bounds.
lessons.instruction: Declare an externally adoptable protocol.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A public protocol and its requirements are visible to importing modules.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A private protocol can't define an external conformance contract.

lessons.title: Extensions and Private Members
lessons.objective: Use private members from same-file extensions.
lessons.instruction: Choose whether a same-file extension can access the original type's private member.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Same-file extensions can access private members of the extended type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift permits this private access across same-file extensions.

lessons.title: Generic and Alias Access
lessons.objective: Limit generics and type aliases by the types in their declarations.
lessons.instruction: Choose the maximum access of an alias to a private type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Generic declarations and type aliases can't expose less-accessible component types.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A public alias would reveal a private underlying type.
lessons.sourceTitle: Access Control · Generics and Type Aliases

levels.title: Level 29 · Advanced Operators
levels.summary: Manipulate bits, define operators, and build declarative result syntax.

lessons.title: Bitwise NOT
lessons.objective: Invert every bit in an integer.
lessons.instruction: Invert initialBits.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ~ flips every bit.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: ! negates a Boolean. Integer bitwise NOT uses ~.

lessons.title: Bitwise AND
lessons.objective: Keep bits set in both operands.
lessons.instruction: Mask firstSixBits with lastSixBits.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. & sets a result bit only when both input bits are set.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: && combines Boolean conditions. Bitwise AND uses &.

lessons.title: Bitwise OR
lessons.objective: Set bits present in either operand.
lessons.instruction: Combine someBits and moreBits bit by bit.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. | sets a bit when either operand contains it.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: || combines Boolean conditions. Bitwise OR uses |.

lessons.title: Bitwise XOR
lessons.objective: Set bits that differ between operands.
lessons.instruction: Combine firstBits and otherBits with exclusive OR.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. ^ sets a bit when exactly one input bit is set.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: | also sets bits present in both operands. XOR uses ^.

lessons.title: Left Shift
lessons.objective: Move unsigned bits left and introduce zeros on the right.
lessons.instruction: Shift one four places left.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. << shifts bits left.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: >> shifts bits right. Use <<.

lessons.title: Signed Right Shift
lessons.objective: Preserve a signed integer's sign while shifting right.
lessons.instruction: Shift negativeEight right by one.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Signed right shift fills vacated high bits from the sign bit.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The requested direction is right, using >>.

lessons.title: Overflow Addition
lessons.objective: Opt into fixed-width wraparound addition.
lessons.instruction: Wrap UInt8.max plus one to zero.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. &+ permits two's-complement wraparound instead of trapping.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Ordinary + traps on overflow. Use &+ for explicit wrapping.

lessons.title: Precedence and Associativity
lessons.objective: Predict grouping from operator precedence.
lessons.instruction: Choose how 2 + 3 * 4 is grouped.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Multiplication has higher precedence than addition.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: * binds before +.

lessons.title: Operator Methods
lessons.objective: Implement an operator as a static type method.
lessons.instruction: Implement unary minus for Vector2D.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Operator implementations are static methods on a participating type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: mutating changes an instance method's self. Operators are declared static.

lessons.title: Prefix Operators
lessons.objective: Declare a custom prefix operator implementation.
lessons.instruction: Mark unary - as a prefix implementation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. prefix distinguishes an operator written before its operand.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: postfix operators follow their operand. Unary - is prefix here.
lessons.sourceTitle: Advanced Operators · Prefix and Postfix Operators

lessons.title: Implementing Compound Assignment
lessons.objective: Implement an assignment operator that mutates its left operand.
lessons.instruction: Declare += with an in-out left side.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Compound assignment mutates the left operand through inout.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: borrowing forbids mutation. Use inout.

lessons.title: Equivalence Operators
lessons.objective: Provide value equality for a custom type.
lessons.instruction: Choose the protocol whose conformance supports == and !=.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Equatable defines value equality and enables != from ==.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Identifiable supplies stable identity, not value equality. Use Equatable.

lessons.title: Custom Operators
lessons.objective: Declare a new operator token before implementing it.
lessons.instruction: Declare +++ as a prefix operator.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A custom operator declaration states its fixity at file scope.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: static belongs on the implementation method. The operator declaration begins with prefix.

lessons.title: Custom Infix Precedence
lessons.objective: Assign a custom infix operator to a precedence group.
lessons.instruction: Declare +- with AdditionPrecedence.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The declaration names a precedence group after the colon.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: left is an associativity value inside a precedencegroup declaration. Name AdditionPrecedence here.
lessons.sourceTitle: Advanced Operators · Precedence for Custom Infix Operators

lessons.title: Result Builder Declaration
lessons.objective: Mark a type as a result builder.
lessons.instruction: Declare DrawingBuilder as a result-builder type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @resultBuilder enables result-building transformation for the type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses @resultBuilder.

lessons.title: Building Components
lessons.objective: Combine statement components into a result.
lessons.instruction: Declare the required component-combining method.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. buildBlock combines components produced by the transformed closure.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The fundamental result-builder operation is buildBlock.

lessons.title: Result-Builder Parameters
lessons.objective: Apply a builder transformation to a closure parameter.
lessons.instruction: Transform the drawing closure with DrawingBuilder.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Apply the concrete builder type to the closure parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @resultBuilder defines a builder type. Use @DrawingBuilder at the call site.

levels.title: Level 30 · Reference: Types and Expressions
levels.summary: Practice lexical and expression forms defined by Swift's formal reference.

lessons.title: Nested Comments
lessons.objective: Use comments as whitespace, including nested multiline comments.
lessons.instruction: Choose a valid nested multiline comment.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Swift multiline comments can nest.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Use balanced /* ... */ delimiters for each nested level.

lessons.title: Escaped Identifiers
lessons.objective: Use a reserved keyword as an identifier when necessary.
lessons.instruction: Name a property repeat despite repeat being a keyword.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Backticks allow a keyword to be used as an identifier.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A quoted value is a String literal. Escape the identifier with backticks.

lessons.title: Regular-Expression Literals
lessons.objective: Create a regex with slash literal syntax.
lessons.instruction: Match one or more decimal digits.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. /.../ creates a Regex literal.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A quoted pattern is a String. Use slash-delimited regex literal syntax.

lessons.title: Metatype Types
lessons.objective: Refer to a type itself as a value.
lessons.instruction: Store the Int type value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Int.self is the value whose type is Int.Type.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Int() constructs an Int instance. Use Int.self for the metatype value.

lessons.title: The Self Type
lessons.objective: Refer to the current conforming or dynamic type in a declaration.
lessons.instruction: Require copy() to return the same conforming type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Self denotes the conforming type in a protocol requirement.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Lowercase self denotes an instance. Use capital Self for the type.

lessons.title: Key-Path Expressions
lessons.objective: Create a type-safe reference to a property.
lessons.instruction: Create a key path from Person to name.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A backslash begins a key-path expression.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: A String doesn't preserve the property's type. Use \Person.name.

lessons.title: Selector Expressions
lessons.objective: Create an Objective-C selector checked from a Swift member reference.
lessons.instruction: Create a selector for Controller.refresh.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #selector forms an Objective-C selector from a compatible member.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #keyPath produces an Objective-C key-path string. Use #selector.

lessons.title: Key-Path String Expressions
lessons.objective: Produce an Objective-C-compatible key-path string.
lessons.instruction: Create the string key path for Person.name.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #keyPath produces the Objective-C key-path String.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #selector produces a method selector. Use #keyPath.

lessons.title: Implicit Pointer Conversion
lessons.objective: Pass contiguous Swift storage temporarily to a pointer parameter.
lessons.instruction: Expose mutable array storage only for the duration of the closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The scoped buffer API bounds the temporary pointer's lifetime.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An implicitly converted pointer must not escape its call. Use the scoped unsafe-buffer API.

lessons.title: Initializer Expressions
lessons.objective: Refer to an initializer as a function value.
lessons.instruction: Store String.init as a callable value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Type.init references an initializer without calling it.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Type.self is a metatype value. Use String.init for the initializer function.

lessons.title: Postfix self
lessons.objective: Disambiguate a member whose name matches a type member or keyword context.
lessons.instruction: Refer explicitly to the enum case named self-like through its type value context.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. postfix .self produces the type value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: .init references initialization. Use .self for the type value.

lessons.title: Wildcard Expressions
lessons.objective: Ignore a value explicitly when its result isn't needed.
lessons.instruction: Discard the returned result intentionally.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. _ explicitly ignores the value.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: nil is a value for optional types. Use _ to discard a result.

levels.title: Level 31 · Reference: Statements and Declarations
levels.summary: Control compilation and use advanced declaration forms.

lessons.title: Conditional Compilation
lessons.objective: Compile source only for a matching platform condition.
lessons.instruction: Compile the branch only on macOS.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #if evaluates a compilation condition before building.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Runtime if requires a Boolean expression in compiled code. Platform compilation uses #if.

lessons.title: Line-Control Statements
lessons.objective: Change compiler-reported source locations for generated code.
lessons.instruction: Set a logical filename and line.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #sourceLocation(file:line:) changes diagnostic source mapping.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #line reads the current line number. Use #sourceLocation to control it.

lessons.title: Compile-Time Diagnostics
lessons.objective: Emit a deliberate compiler warning or error.
lessons.instruction: Stop compilation with a custom diagnostic.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #error emits a compile-time error.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #warning reports without necessarily stopping compilation. Use #error.

lessons.title: Availability Conditions
lessons.objective: Guard APIs by runtime platform availability.
lessons.instruction: Enter the branch only when iOS 26 or newer is available.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. #available succeeds when the listed version requirements are met.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: #unavailable tests the inverse. Use #available for the new-API branch.

lessons.title: Import Declarations
lessons.objective: Bring another module's declarations into scope.
lessons.instruction: Import Foundation.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. import exposes declarations from another module.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift uses import, not include.

lessons.title: Borrowing Parameters
lessons.objective: Use a noncopying value temporarily without consuming it.
lessons.instruction: Promise that inspect doesn't consume value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. borrowing provides temporary read access and leaves ownership with the caller.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: consuming transfers ownership. Use borrowing to preserve the caller's value.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Borrowing and Consuming Parameters

lessons.title: Consuming Parameters
lessons.objective: Transfer ownership of a value into a function.
lessons.instruction: Allow store to consume its noncopyable value.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. consuming transfers ownership to the callee.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: borrowing doesn't transfer ownership. Use consuming.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Borrowing and Consuming Parameters

lessons.title: callAsFunction
lessons.objective: Make an instance callable with function-call syntax.
lessons.instruction: Declare the specially named method used by instance().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. callAsFunction enables direct call syntax on an instance.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Swift recognizes the special name callAsFunction.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Methods with Special Names

lessons.title: Rethrowing Functions
lessons.objective: Propagate errors only when a function parameter throws.
lessons.instruction: Declare mapValues as conditionally throwing through its transform.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. rethrows restricts errors to those thrown by a function parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: throws allows independent errors from the body. Use rethrows for conditional propagation.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Rethrowing Functions and Methods

lessons.title: Functions That Never Return
lessons.objective: Declare control flow that cannot return normally.
lessons.instruction: Choose the return type for fatalFailure().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Never has no values and marks a function that doesn't return.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Void returns normally with (). Use Never for nonreturning control flow.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Functions That Never Return

lessons.title: Generic Protocol Dispatch
lessons.objective: Recognize that generic code uses protocol requirements, not same-named extension-only overloads.
lessons.instruction: Choose which implementation generic code can dispatch through a T: P constraint.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Generic constrained dispatch uses the protocol requirement witness.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: An extension-only overload isn't a protocol requirement and isn't dynamically selected through T: P.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Overridden Requirements in Generic Contexts

lessons.title: Nonredundant Conformance
lessons.objective: Declare each protocol conformance exactly once.
lessons.instruction: Choose the valid conformance layout.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. A type must not declare redundant conformances to the same protocol.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Duplicate conformance declarations are invalid even if implementations differ.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Protocol Conformance Must Not Be Redundant

levels.title: Level 32 · Reference: Attributes
levels.summary: Apply compiler-known behaviors to declarations, types, and switch cases.

lessons.title: @available
lessons.objective: Declare the platform versions where an API can be used.
lessons.instruction: Make NewFeature available starting in iOS 26.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @available declares API availability by platform version.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @backDeployed supplies an implementation on older systems. Availability is declared with @available.

lessons.title: @backDeployed
lessons.objective: Emit a public implementation into clients for older platform versions.
lessons.instruction: Back-deploy an API before iOS 27.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @backDeployed(before:) lets clients carry a compatible implementation until the platform supplies it.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @inlinable exposes a body for optimization. Back deployment uses @backDeployed.

lessons.title: @discardableResult
lessons.objective: Permit callers to ignore a non-Void result without a warning.
lessons.instruction: Allow update() calls that intentionally ignore the returned count.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @discardableResult suppresses unused-result warnings for the declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @unchecked applies to supported protocol conformance. Use @discardableResult.

lessons.title: @dynamicCallable
lessons.objective: Route call syntax to dynamicallyCall methods.
lessons.instruction: Make ScriptObject callable with arguments.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @dynamicCallable forwards instance(...) to dynamicallyCall.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @dynamicMemberLookup handles unresolved members. Call syntax uses @dynamicCallable.

lessons.title: @dynamicMemberLookup
lessons.objective: Resolve unknown member names through a subscript.
lessons.instruction: Enable dynamic member lookup on JSONValue.
lessons.codeSuffix: struct JSONValue { subscript(dynamicMember name: String) -> String { name } }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @dynamicMemberLookup forwards unresolved member access to a dynamicMember subscript.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @dynamicCallable handles call syntax. Member lookup uses @dynamicMemberLookup.

lessons.title: Export Attribute
lessons.objective: Choose whether client modules receive an interface symbol or an implementation body.
lessons.instruction: Choose the export argument that exposes a callable symbol while hiding the function body.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. The interface argument exports a callable symbol without exposing the body to clients.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: implementation exports the body without emitting a callable symbol. Choose interface.

lessons.title: @frozen
lessons.objective: Commit a public enum or structure layout as ABI-stable.
lessons.instruction: Promise a public enum won't gain cases without breaking compatibility.
lessons.codeSuffix: public enum Direction { case north, south }
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @frozen exposes a fixed layout or case set across module evolution.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @available controls platform versions. Layout commitment uses @frozen.

lessons.title: @inlinable
lessons.objective: Expose a function body to importing modules for optimization.
lessons.instruction: Allow client modules to inline calculate().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @inlinable serializes the body into the module interface for clients.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @usableFromInline exposes an internal declaration to inlinable bodies. Mark the public function @inlinable.

lessons.title: @main
lessons.objective: Choose a program's type-based entry point.
lessons.instruction: Make SwiftLearnApp the application entry type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @main identifies the type containing the program entry point.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @main is the general modern type-entry attribute.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · main and Application-Main Attributes

lessons.title: Objective-C Exposure
lessons.objective: Expose or suppress Objective-C entry points deliberately.
lessons.instruction: Expose refresh() to the Objective-C runtime.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @objc exposes a compatible declaration to Objective-C.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @nonobjc suppresses Objective-C exposure. Use @objc.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · objc and nonobjc Attributes

lessons.title: @objcMembers
lessons.objective: Infer Objective-C exposure for eligible class members.
lessons.instruction: Expose compatible members of LegacyController by default.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @objcMembers infers @objc for eligible members of the class and extensions.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @objc on the class alone doesn't apply the same member-wide inference. Use @objcMembers.

lessons.title: @NSCopying
lessons.objective: Copy an Objective-C-compatible property value on assignment.
lessons.instruction: Give attachment copy semantics in an NSObject subclass.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @NSCopying uses copyWithZone: when setting the property.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @NSManaged delegates storage to Core Data. Copy semantics use @NSCopying.

lessons.title: @NSManaged
lessons.objective: Declare Core Data-provided storage and implementation.
lessons.instruction: Mark a managed object's name property as implemented by Core Data.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @NSManaged tells the compiler Core Data supplies the implementation at runtime.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @NSCopying changes assignment semantics. Core Data properties use @NSManaged.

lessons.title: @preconcurrency
lessons.objective: Stage concurrency checking for declarations from older concurrency models.
lessons.instruction: Import LegacyKit with preconcurrency compatibility.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @preconcurrency suppresses certain strict concurrency diagnostics for the imported API.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @Sendable applies to function types and closures. Compatibility imports use @preconcurrency.

lessons.title: @unchecked Sendable
lessons.objective: Take manual responsibility for a conformance the compiler can't verify.
lessons.instruction: Declare manually synchronized Cache as Sendable.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @unchecked disables compiler enforcement for Sendable; correctness becomes the author's responsibility.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @preconcurrency stages checking. Manual Sendable responsibility uses @unchecked.

lessons.title: @usableFromInline
lessons.objective: Allow an internal declaration to be referenced by inlinable code.
lessons.instruction: Expose internal helper() to an @inlinable body without making it public API.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @usableFromInline makes the symbol ABI-visible to inlinable code while retaining internal source access.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The helper itself need not expose its body for inlining. Use @usableFromInline.

lessons.title: @warn_unqualified_access
lessons.objective: Warn when a potentially ambiguous API is called without qualification.
lessons.instruction: Require callers to prefer instance-qualified min().
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @warn_unqualified_access diagnoses calls lacking a module, type, or instance qualifier.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @discardableResult controls unused returns. Qualification warnings use @warn_unqualified_access.

lessons.title: @convention
lessons.objective: Specify the calling convention of a function type.
lessons.instruction: Declare a C-compatible callback type.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @convention(c) gives the function type a C calling convention.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @escaping controls closure lifetime. Calling convention uses @convention.

lessons.title: @Sendable Function Types
lessons.objective: Require closure captures and behavior safe for concurrent transfer.
lessons.instruction: Declare work as a sendable closure.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @Sendable constrains the function value for concurrency transfer.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @MainActor isolates execution. Transfer-safe function types use @Sendable.

lessons.title: @unknown default
lessons.objective: Handle future enum cases while retaining compiler warnings for known omissions.
lessons.instruction: Provide a fallback for enum cases introduced by future SDKs.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @unknown default handles future cases and warns when a known case is omitted.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Plain default suppresses the future-case diagnostic benefit. Use @unknown default.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · unknown Switch Case Attribute

levels.title: Level 33 · Reference: Specialized Syntax
levels.summary: Practice integer generics and framework-facing declaration attributes.

lessons.title: Integer Generic Parameters
lessons.objective: Parameterize a generic declaration with an integer value.
lessons.instruction: Declare x as an Int generic value parameter.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. let x: Int declares an integer generic parameter.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: Integer generic parameters use the let keyword inside the generic parameter clause.

lessons.title: Required Stored-Property Defaults
lessons.objective: Understand the requires_stored_property_inits attribute's class invariant.
lessons.instruction: Choose what the attribute requires from every stored property in the class.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. Every stored property must provide a default value as part of its declaration.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: The attribute requires declaration-site defaults, not lazy storage.

lessons.title: Interface Builder Attributes
lessons.objective: Expose compatible declarations to Interface Builder tooling.
lessons.instruction: Make title editable in Interface Builder's inspector.
lessons.correctFeedback: Correct. @IBInspectable exposes a compatible property in the inspector.
lessons.incorrectFeedback: @IBAction exposes a method connection. Inspector-editable properties use @IBInspectable.
lessons.sourceTitle: Language Reference · Interface Builder Declaration Attributes
